'''Miha Valič''' (4 November 1978 – 5 October 2008) was a [[Slovenia]]n [[Mountaineering|mountaineer]]. He was the first person to ascend every [[List of mountains of the Alps|4000-meter peak]] in the [[Alps]] in one winter session.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.alpinist.com/doc/ALP19/newswire-valic-alps-4000-meter |title=4000m Winter Alps marathon completed in 102 days |publisher=Alpinist.com |date=2007-03-16 |accessdate=2008-06-10}}</ref> The Alps marathon was completed in 102 days.

Valič attended 10 [[exploration|expeditions]], mostly in [[Yosemite]], [[Patagonia]] and the [[Himalayas]]. In 2003, Valič spent two months in the [[Yosemite Valley]] with [[Matjaž Jeran]], where they free climbed the [[El Capitan]] rock formation's Freerider route (1200 m, 5.12d/13a). A year later, he made the first alpine-style ascent on route Eternal Flame in [[Trango Towers|Trango]] group with [[Tomaž Jakofčič]] and [[Klemen Mali]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.alpinist.com/doc/ALP17/newswire-trango |title=Slovenian bonaza in the Trango group |publisher=Alpinist.com |date=2006-09-28 |accessdate=2008-06-10}}</ref> Valič was also a successful [[sport climber]]. He climbed routes up to 8b+.

On 5 October 2008, Valič died while descending [[Cho Oyu]] after a successful ascent.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.sta.si/en/vest.php?id=1326190 |title=Slovenian Climber Killed in Himalayas |publisher=Slovenian Press Agency |date=2006-10-06 |accessdate=2008-06-10}}</ref>
